transcript:
This message comes from Google Workspace with Gemini, one subscription that does it all.
Personalized AI and premium business versions of Gmail, Google Docs, Drive and more.
Try it free for 14 days at goo.gle/workspacewithgemini.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman. The government will release its latest reports
on the nation's employment picture this morning. And Pierre Scott Horsley tells us what economists
are considering. They think the report's going to show that hiring picked up a bit in October after
a pretty anemic month in September when employers added only 29,000 jobs. Today's report's expected
to show that employers added somewhere around 60,000 jobs in October. That's not what you would
call robust growth, but it is enough to keep the unemployment rate low. And so long as that's the
case and the job market remains stable, the Federal Reserve is able to focus its attention on
fighting inflation. NPR's Scott Horsley reporting. Separately, investors have been reacting to the
midterm elections. Democrats will decisively control Congress next term. They'll expect they'll
review regulation of the AI industry, while voters in several states chose to limit data centers.
This weighed on the tech-heavy NASDAQ index. It lost well over 5 percent yesterday.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth says efforts to impeach him will fail. NPR's Quill Lawrence
reports a Republican congressman has been pushing to impeach Hegseth since well before the elections.
Speculation that President Trump might fire Hegseth over the war in Iran is widespread.
Outgoing Kentucky Republican Thomas Massey said Hegseth should be impeached for how he's conducted
that war. In a five-minute video posted on social media, Hegseth compares himself to Trump.
A disgruntled defeated congressman along with all his Democrat allies has also dropped sham
articles of impeachment against yours truly, just like they tried against President Trump
twice. Didn't work against President Trump, and it won't work with me.
Congressman Massey posted in response that his impeachment resolution is likely to be
kinder to Hegseth than what the Democrats would do in January. Even Republican sources on Capitol
Hill say Hegseth is deeply unpopular. Quill Lawrence, NPR News.
President Trump says he is close to a deal with Russia. It's aimed at ending the war in Ukraine.
The president's claim came after he met with a senior Kremlin representative at the White House
yesterday. NPR's Charles Mains has more from Moscow. Speaking to the press corps in the Oval
Office, Trump acknowledged he met to discuss peace efforts with Kremlin envoy Kirill Dimitrov,
who was in Washington for a separate event celebrating First Lady Melania Trump's
humanitarian efforts in Ukraine. Trump said he did not meet with Ukrainian representatives,
also present for Mrs. Trump's event, but said the peace deal could involve not only Ukraine,
but all of Europe. It's going to be a big, beautiful agreement, and everyone's going to
be thrilled. While Trump has repeatedly overstated progress on negotiations to end the war,
his comments come as his administration has recently re-upped its diplomatic efforts,
with U.S.-led peace talks between Russia and Ukraine scheduled in Abu Dhabi next week.
Charles Mains, NPR News, Moscow. You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
European authorities say more bomb threats have been made against European passenger flights today.
Many planes were threatened yesterday and earlier this week. It's not clear who's making the threats.
Today's affected flights have involved Czechia and are aimed at both incoming and outgoing planes.
The upstart professional LIV Golf Association is ending operations. It pitched itself as an
alternative to the PGA Tour's rigid pay structure and practices. Steve Futterman explains it failed
to gain traction. When it began in 2022 with backing from Saudi Arabia, LIV went on a spending
spree, taking big-name golfers away from a PGA with huge bonuses. Phil Mickelson was reportedly
given a $200 million deal. Other big names included John Rahm, Dustin Johnson, and Sergio Garcia.
But despite the Saudi Public Investment Fund spending around $5 billion, it never caught on.
Attendance at tournaments and TV ratings were low. Attempts to merge with a PGA failed.
Last year, the Saudi funding began to dry up. In September, LIV filed for bankruptcy.
Lawyers representing the group say it has started the process of winding down operations.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman in Los Angeles. The estate of the late singer Dolly Parton is
dropping a complaint against her nephew, who had also served as Parton's security chief. No reason
has been given for this move. The manager of Parton's estate had originally accused the nephew
of making threats, an allegation the nephew strongly denied. This is NPR.
[BLANK_AUDIO]

topics.text: Jobs report expected to show about 60,000 October hiring gains after weak September
Tech-heavy NASDAQ falls over 5% after midterm elections, investors react to AI regulation outlook
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth dismisses impeachment efforts; Rep. Thomas Massie pushes impeachment over Iran war
President Trump says he is close to Russia deal to end Ukraine war after Kremlin envoy meeting
European authorities report new bomb threats against passenger flights, including Czechia-linked flights
LIV Golf Association begins winding down operations after failing to gain traction against PGA Tour
Estate of Dolly Parton drops complaint against her nephew and former security chief
